articles.title: President Murmu appoints new governors for 6 states; 4 new, 2 moved
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu has appointed new governors for six states.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu has appointed new governors for six states. Om Prakash Mathur, who was serving as governor of Sikkim, has been appointed governor of Kerala. Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, who is the present governor of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, will be relieved of his position. Dushyant Gautam has been appointed the new governor of Sikkim.The appointments also include changes in Odisha, Karnataka and Uttarakhand.Braj Mohan Ram has been appointed governor of Odisha. Dr Sudha Yadav will take over as governor of Karnataka. Dr Dhal Singh Bisen has been named governor of Uttarakhand.The changes in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Sikkim involve the movement of two serving governors and the appointment of a new governor. Mathur will move from Sikkim to Keralam, while Arlekar will leave Keralam to take charge in Tamil Nadu. Gautam will succeed Mathur in Sikkim.With these appointments, the gubernatorial leadership will change in all six states. Keralam will have Mathur as its new governor, while Tamil Nadu will have Arlekar. Gautam will take over in Sikkim. Ram, Yadav and Bisen will assume the gubernatorial roles in Odisha, Karnataka and Uttarakhand, respectively.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Delhi's new protest venue Ramlila Maidan has just 3 dates available this year - check details
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ramlila Maidan, newly designated as one of the capital's three protest sites, is already booked for most of the next two-and-a-half months,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ramlila Maidan, newly designated as one of the capital's three protest sites, is already booked for most of the next two-and-a-half months, leaving just three days available for reservations this year.Additionally, while a small section of the ground can be used for protests free of charge, booking the larger venue, which spans 12 acres and can accommodate up to 50,000 people, involves a daily fee and a refundable security deposit.Revealing that only December 29, 30 and 31 as the availiable dates, an official quoted by PTI said, "The booking rate for the ground is Rs 50,000 per day, plus a Rs 55,000 security deposit that is refundable. The initial outlay including taxes comes to Rs 1.21 lakh for a day's booking."However, officials clarified that a small portion of the ground, with space for around 150 people, remains available for protests and gatherings free of charge.Permission to use the larger ground must be obtained from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi's horticulture department, which processes bookings after applicants secure a no-objection certificate from Delhi Police.The arrangement has drawn criticism from opposition leaders and protesters, who argue that the limited availability and high booking costs could make demonstrations difficult to organise.AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj questioned the decision, pointing to events already scheduled at the venue. Govt. played another fraud with its citizens. The Ramleela Maidan is occupied with two Ramleelas," Bharadwaj wrote on X."How can one hold a protest here? Do they want to create chaos?" he asked.Protesters also highlighted the financial burden, noting that demonstrations at Jantar Mantar did not require comparable payments.Civic officials, however, pointed to the revenue implications of allowing unrestricted use of the ground. "If given up for protest without any fees, the civic body will stand to lose at least Rs 50,000 plus per day," an official said, quoted by PTI.The ground is frequently reserved for public events and religious festivities, particularly around Dussehra and Diwali, contributing to the shortage of available dates.Apart from booking constraints, the venue presents traffic-management challenges. Located in a busy commercial area near three hospitals and municipal offices, Ramlila Maidan has witnessed major congestion during political rallies and other large gatherings.Officials said police often have to introduce one-way traffic restrictions on Asaf Ali Road and divert vehicles towards Jawaharlal Nehru Marg. A BJP rally in 2014 reportedly caused traffic jams extending nearly four kilometres to ITO, despite being held on a Sunday.The venue has been central to Delhi's political history for decades. Once a pond, the site was filled and levelled around 1930 to accommodate Ramlila performances, which began there in 1932. It subsequently hosted major political gatherings addressed by leaders including Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, Jayaprakash Narayan and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.On June 25, 1975, the day the Emergency was declared, Jayaprakash Narayan and Vajpayee addressed a rally at the ground. Relatively recently, Arvind Kejriwal took oath as Delhi chief minister there in 2013.The controversy follows an standing order issued by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, which removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest venues and identified Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as the three new locations for demonstrations. Police said a detailed, revised standard operating procedure for protests at these sites would be issued separately.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1937, Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific; 89 years later, a 17-member expedition has set out on an 830-nautical-mile voyage to Nikumaroro to inspect a lagoon anomaly visible in aerial photos from 1938
articles.summary: Nearly nine decades after Amelia Earhart vanished somewhere over the Pacific, the search for her aircraft has entered another chapter.
articles.body: Nearly nine decades after Amelia Earhart vanished somewhere over the Pacific, the search for her aircraft has entered another chapter. A 17-member team backed by Purdue University has sailed towards the remote island of Nikumaroro, following a potentially significant clue hidden in its lagoon states an online report by Reuters. The expedition hopes to determine whether an unusual object visible in aerial and satellite imagery could be part of Earhart’s missing Lockheed Electra 10-E.A mystery that began in 1937As per Reuters, Earhart disappeared on July 2, 1937, while attempting to fly around the world. She and navigator Fred Noonan were travelling from Papua New Guinea toward Howland Island, a tiny Pacific atoll intended to be their next refuelling stop, the report adds.The Electra never arrived. After the aircraft’s final communications, which indicated dwindling fuel and gave its last known position, a massive search operation failed to locate either the plane or its crew. The official US government position has long held that the aircraft ran out of fuel and crashed into the Pacific near Howland Island. Another theory, however, has continued to attract researchers: Earhart and Noonan may have landed on Nikumaroro, formerly known as Gardner Island, and survived for a time as castaways, also states the online report.The lagoon anomalyThe new expedition, led by marine archaeologist Richard Pettigrew of the Archaeological Legacy Institute in collaboration with Purdue, is focused on an unusual shape identified in imagery of Nikumaroro. The object, first noticed in a 2020 satellite image, has a branching form that researchers believe could resemble an aircraft fuselage and wings. The team has also found indications that a similar feature may appear in aerial photographs dating back to 1938, only months after Earhart disappeared, state the October 10 report by Reuters.The expedition travelled roughly 830 nautical miles to reach the uninhabited island in the Phoenix Islands, part of the Republic of Kiribati. Once there, researchers are expected to spend five days investigating the lagoon before beginning a six-day return journey to Tarawa.A theory with a long historyThe Nikumaroro hypothesis is not new. Explorer Ric Gillespie and the International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery have spent decades investigating the island and have uncovered objects that supporters believe could be linked to Earhart, including a 1930s-era cosmetic container and remnants of a pocketknife.As per the report, radio transmission records and an old photograph of the island have also been cited as possible clues. Yet earlier searches for the aircraft in surrounding waters have failed, including a 2019 expedition led by marine archaeologist Robert Ballard. Gillespie believes the aircraft may have initially landed on the reef before eventually being swept into deeper water by tides and surf.Tree or aircraft?The latest clue has its own controversy. Critics of the new expedition argue that the strange shape is not an aircraft at all but a fallen pandanus tree, whose roots and branches can create an appearance remarkably similar to the object visible in the imagery, explains the online report. That disagreement will ultimately be settled, if at all, by what researchers find on the ground and beneath the water.The expedition, costing about $900,000, represents another attempt to resolve one of aviation history’s most enduring mysteries. Purdue has a particularly strong connection to Earhart, who worked at the university as a women's career counsellor and adviser to its aeronautics department and used university support while developing her Electra.Images Courtesy: Wikipedia and Purdue UniversityYou use AI every day. articles.title: Jack Johnson's 2026 tour is matching donations to a Florida creative-reuse charity; how the money supports community education
articles.summary: Jack Johnson’s 2026 SURFILMUSIC Tour is supporting Resource Depot, a creative-reuse and environmental education centre in Palm Beach County, Florida,
articles.body: Jack Johnson’s 2026 SURFILMUSIC Tour is supporting Resource Depot, a creative-reuse and environmental education centre in Palm Beach County, Florida, through its All At Once initiative. The Johnson Ohana Foundation will match donations to the charity dollar-for-dollar, up to $2,500, through 15 November 2026. The funds will support Resource Depot’s creative-reuse education and community programmes. The organisation is also scheduled to participate in the All At Once Nonprofit Village at iTHINK Financial Amphitheatre on 18 August 2026, where visitors can meet its team, see a surfboard community art installation and learn about creative reuse.How is Jack Johnson’s 2026 tour supporting Florida charityAccording to Resource Depot, the matching scheme allows donations made through Resource Depot’s All At Once donation form to be matched by the Johnson Ohana Foundation. The foundation will match donations dollar-for-dollar, subject to a maximum matching amount of $2,500 and a deadline of 15 November 2026. Resource Depot’s donation form lists preset contribution amounts of $10, $25, $50, $100, $250 and $500, alongside an option to enter a different amount. The appeal identifies creative-reuse education and community programmes as the intended beneficiaries. The match is part of the foundation’s wider support for the All At Once network, which works with non-profit organisations at stops on Johnson’s tour.How Depot promotes creative reuse and environmental educationResource Depot describes itself as Palm Beach County’s creative reuse and environmental education centre. Its work centres on creative reuse and helping the community understand how materials can be used in new ways. The organisation’s announcement of the tour partnership says it wants to encourage concertgoers to see waste as a resource for creativity and positive change.The donation appeal links the matching offer directly to the organisation’s education and community programmes. The purpose of the campaign is to help fund Resource Depot’s existing creative-reuse and community work.What visitors could see at the All At Once Nonprofit VillageResource Depot’s announcement identifies 18 August 2026 as the date it would participate in the All At Once Nonprofit Village at iTHINK Financial Amphitheatre in West Palm Beach. The organisation said visitors would be able to meet its team, view a completed surfboard community art installation and learn about creative reuse.The planned appearance is part of All At Once’s approach to connecting audiences with local non-profit groups at concert venues. According to Jack Johnson’s official 2026 greening page, it encourages fans to engage with participating organisations, donate, volunteer or become members. Resource Depot’s scheduled presence was intended to introduce concertgoers to its environmental education work and explain how creative reuse can contribute to more sustainable practices.How Jack Johnson’s 2026 tour promotes sustainabilityThe donation partnership sits within the broader sustainability programme for Johnson’s 2026 SURFILMUSIC Tour. The official tour website identifies plastic-free initiatives and sustainable local food systems as key areas of its environmental work. It also encourages concertgoers to take practical steps, including choosing reusable items, refilling bottles at designated water stations and sorting waste into the appropriate recycling and composting bins.Other measures include using biodiesel blends for tour trucks, buses and generators, transporting equipment by ground and sea where applicable, and working with venues to reduce disposable plastic. The programme also describes a farm-to-stage approach to sourcing locally grown organic food and arrangements to donate leftover food from shows to community hunger-relief organisations through Musically Fed. These are tour-wide initiatives rather than activities funded specifically by Resource Depot’s donation appeal.How All At Once connects concertgoers with local non-profitsAll At Once allows participating organisations to reach concertgoers through local environmental projects and community engagement. Johnson’s official tour information says the Johnson Ohana Foundation provides direct and matching donations to the network’s non-profit partners. Supporters can also volunteer, become members or engage with organisations at the Village Green during shows.The specific financial commitment is the dollar-for-dollar match of donations up to $2,500 through 15 November 2026. articles.title: 'No elevated risk’: US homeland security chief defends plan to livestream Nidal Hasan’s execution
articles.summary: US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has defended the Trump administration’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, the former US
articles.body: US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has defended the Trump administration’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, the former US Army major convicted of killing 13 soldiers at Fort Hood in Texas, dismissing concerns that the broadcast could fuel radicalisation or turn him into a martyr.“I don’t see an elevated risk at this point at all because of this,” Mullin said in an interview with CBS News’ Face the Nation on Sunday.“If you attack America, we will come after you, and we will make sure that the punishment fits the crime,” he added.Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3 for the 2009 shooting at Fort Hood, in which 13 people were killed and 32 others injured.The plan to broadcast his execution live, announced by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth last week, has drawn criticism from both Republicans and Democrats. President Donald Trump has backed the idea but has not made a final decision on whether the execution will be televised.Mullin said the administration had considered the potential risks and argued that viewers would not be forced to watch the broadcast.“No one has to watch it if they don’t choose to,” he told CBS News.However, critics have warned that broadcasting the execution could give extremist groups propaganda material and increase security risks for Americans at home and abroad.Alaska Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski called the proposal “gruesome”, arguing that it could give Hasan the martyrdom he sought.“It's something I would expect from terrorists and dictators, but not here in America,” she wrote on X, adding that the way the US carries out justice matters as much as the justice itself.Virginia Democratic Senator Mark Warner also cautioned that a public execution could provide terrorist organisations with a propaganda victory, fuel radicalisation and put American service members, diplomats and citizens overseas at greater risk.Hasan, who was shot during the attack and now uses a wheelchair, admitted to killing the unarmed troops at a crowded medical facility at Fort Hood. During his trial, he said he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military.If carried out, Hasan’s execution would be the first by the US military since 1961 and its first firing-squad execution since World War II. A public broadcast would also mark the first public execution in the United States in nearly a century.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US threatens to cut Ukraine intelligence, weapons supplies over Russian energy strikes
articles.summary: The United States has threatened to suspend intelligence sharing with Ukraine and halt European purchases of American weapons for Kyiv unless Ukrainian
articles.body: The United States has threatened to suspend intelligence sharing with Ukraine and halt European purchases of American weapons for Kyiv unless Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stops attacks on Russian energy facilities, CNN reported, citing two European officials.The reported warning comes as US President Donald Trump says Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an “energy ceasefire”, even as Zelenskyy accuses Moscow of continuing attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Russia, meanwhile, has yet to explicitly confirm that it has accepted the proposed arrangement.According to two European officials cited by CNN, the US administration has warned Ukraine and its European allies that Washington could suspend intelligence sharing and halt a mechanism through which European countries purchase American weapons for Kyiv. The warnings were reportedly conveyed over the weekend by the State Department and the Pentagon, including through direct communications between the US military and Ukrainian commanders.A US official said American negotiators had reminded Kyiv that Washington was providing weapons and intelligence and that Ukraine should not take actions that hurt American consumers. Another source familiar with the matter said the US had threatened to cut intelligence sharing. The Financial Times first reported the threats.The reported warnings come amid Trump's anger over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries, which have added to tensions between the US president and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Trump has repeatedly called for both countries to stop targeting energy facilities, citing the impact of the war on global fuel prices. Those pressures have been compounded by the US war with Iran.The potential suspension of support could have serious consequences for Ukraine. American intelligence helps its forces detect incoming Russian ballistic missiles and identify launch sites, giving them more time to respond. A halt to weapons purchases under the Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL), a mechanism through which Nato allies finance the purchase of US arms for Ukraine, could also affect supplies of Patriot interceptor missiles, which Kyiv needs to defend against intensifying Russian missile and drone attacks.A Nato official told CNN on Monday that weapons supplies through PURL were continuing. The US had previously suspended intelligence sharing with Ukraine in March 2025 after a heated meeting between Trump and Zelenskyy at the White House. Sharing resumed after Kyiv agreed to a proposed US ceasefire during talks in Saudi Arabia.Against this backdrop, Trump announced on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to what he called an “energy ceasefire”, offering little detail about its terms. The announcement appeared to catch Kyiv by surprise, while Moscow has yet to explicitly confirm that it has accepted the arrangement.Zelenskyy says Russia continued attacks Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukraine was prepared to stop attacking Russian energy infrastructure but accused Moscow of continuing to strike Ukrainian energy facilities even after Trump's announcement.Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland, Zelenskyy said Ukraine had been “horribly surprised” by Russian strikes on a power plant in Kharkiv, a gas production facility and a civilian gas station in the hours after the US president announced the proposed ceasefire.The Ukrainian president later told Fox News Channel's “America’s Newsroom” that Kyiv had refrained from attacking Russian energy sites since Sunday's announcement and was ready to honour the arrangement. He described the proposed halt to energy attacks as “a good first step” towards ending the war.But Zelenskyy expressed doubt over whether Russian President Vladimir Putin would reciprocate.“I’m not sure that (Russian President Vladimir) Putin is ready,” he said.“Even after yesterday’s messages from (Trump) ... Putin attacked our gas infrastructure,” Zelenskyy said. “When we speak about energy ceasefire, it means only one thing: that they don’t attack our energy infrastructure and we don’t respond on their energy infrastructure.”Trump's announcement on social media had declared that the ceasefire took effect immediately, adding, “Do not break it!” However, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined on Monday to confirm whether Moscow had agreed to the arrangement, saying only that “Contacts are ongoing".Zelenskyy's comments came amid a separate dispute over elections in Ukraine. Trump recently suggested that Kyiv should choose a new leader, prompting the Ukrainian president to say that a 60-day ceasefire could allow Ukraine to hold presidential elections.Zelenskyy has argued that elections are currently unfeasible because of continued Russian attacks. He has called for a “full ceasefire”, saying the security situation makes it impossible to organise a vote while strikes continue day and night.Lavrov says Ukraine does not deserve respiteRussia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov pushed back against Zelenskyy's position, arguing that a ceasefire would give Ukraine time to replenish its military supplies with help from European countries.Speaking at a news conference, Lavrov claimed that European countries would use any pause in fighting to “pump [Ukraine] with new weapons” so that Kyiv could continue the war.He also dismissed Zelenskyy's surprise at Trump's announcement, describing the Ukrainian leader's reaction as “fake”. Lavrov accused Zelenskyy of exploiting diplomatic initiatives to secure a temporary break in hostilities rather than pursue a lasting settlement."I don't think he deserves a respite," Lavrov said, adding, "I don't think we will again buy into these assurances and promises."The opposing statements underline the uncertainty surrounding the proposed energy ceasefire. While Kyiv says it is willing to stop attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, Moscow has not clearly committed to the same terms. Meanwhile, Washington's reported threats to restrict intelligence and weapons support have added another layer of pressure on Ukraine as it seeks to defend its territory and maintain Western backing.For now, Trump's announcement has not translated into a clearly agreed and mutually observed halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, leaving the prospects for a wider ceasefire uncertain.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Made right choice, America first': Trump defends Russia diesel deal amid bipartisan backlash
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Monday defended his decision to allow Russian diesel supplies to the United States, saying his administration had acted in
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Monday defended his decision to allow Russian diesel supplies to the United States, saying his administration had acted in the interests of the American people. He also accused the media of ignoring the European Union's energy payments to Moscow, as Ukraine criticised the deal and the EU announced fresh sanctions against Russia.In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump claimed that the European Union had paid Russia $250 billion for energy and accused the media of avoiding the issue."The European Union paid Russia 250 Billion Dollars for Energy, and the Fake News Media doesn’t want to get near that story," Trump wrote.Defending his energy policy, he added, "I made the right choice for the American People — ALWAYS, AMERICA FIRST!"The remarks come amid criticism of the proposed Russian diesel supplies, which Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has argued could help Moscow finance its war against Ukraine.Zelenskyy criticises deal as EU announces fresh sanctionsZelenskyy welcomed the European Union's latest sanctions against Russia, describing them as the "right and necessary signal" towards ending the conflict. He thanked European Council President António Costa, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and EU member states for adopting the measures.The European Council said the new package targets 1,569 individuals and entities linked to Russia's military-industrial network. These include 826 Russian companies and 743 individuals serving as their chief executive officers.The latest measures bring the total number of individuals and entities listed under the EU sanctions regime supporting Ukraine's territorial integrity to nearly 4,600.The sanctions focus on mid-level suppliers that play a key role in Russia's military-industrial network. These companies collectively generate an annual turnover of at least 20 billion euros and employ more than 250,000 people, according to the European Council.EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said sustained economic pressure on Moscow was necessary to end the war. The latest sanctions also target individuals linked to elections held in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories.Zelenskyy linked the sanctions to renewed Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. He said the strikes came a day after Trump announced an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine, claiming both sides had agreed to it."It is becoming increasingly clear that Russia does not want to agree to the energy ceasefire proposed by the United States and intends to continue its terrorist air attacks against our people and communities. Just today, the Russians attacked six energy facilities in Ukraine. Across the country, 33 people were injured. This is what happens when Russia sees the prospect of increasing revenues for its war machine," Zelenskyy said.The Ukrainian president has argued that the proposed diesel deal could increase Moscow's revenues and strengthen its ability to continue the war, which has lasted more than four years.Trump announces large Russian diesel suppliesTrump announced the proposed diesel deal on Friday in a post on Truth Social. He said Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel to the United States, followed by another 500,000 tonnes during November.He added that a further one million tonnes would be supplied immediately afterwards, with another three million tonnes expected within a short period, depending on the condition of Russia's diesel refineries.Trump described the arrangement as a "big deal" and thanked Russian President Vladimir Putin for agreeing to supply what he called "massive amounts" of diesel."I think you heard about the oil deal with Russia. That is a big deal. That is massive amounts of oil coming into our country. I want to thank President Putin. We have massive amounts of oil coming into our country, and it is diesel, which is what we want," Trump told reporters outside the White House before leaving for Syracuse, New York, for the midterm election campaign.Putin says Russian supplies could benefit global economyPutin has also defended the proposed energy supplies, saying they could benefit the global economy.According to the Russian Foreign Ministry, the Russian president made the remarks following a telephone conversation with Trump on Friday. The two leaders discussed Ukraine and Iran, as well as the global energy situation."In discussing the global energy situation, Russia reaffirmed its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the US and global markets. I am confident that this will have a positive impact on the entire global economy," Putin said.The proposed deal has highlighted the contrasting approaches of Washington and Brussels towards Russian energy supplies. While Trump has defended the arrangement on the grounds of American interests, the EU has continued to tighten economic pressure on Moscow over its war against Ukraine.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Nikki Haley's son Nalin Haley once again doubled down on his anti-immigrant stance and said that legal immigration too, does not make any sense at a time
articles.body: Nikki Haley's son Nalin Haley once again doubled down on his anti-immigrant stance and said that legal immigration too, does not make any sense at a time when companies are not hiring. Legal immigrants are those who legally come to the US on a study visa or a work visa. The comment came at a time when the Donald Trump administration unleashed an unprecedented crackdown on H-1B visa program, leading to Green Cards. But Nalin's comment was in the context of Vivek Ramaswamy's stance on immigration, an old statement that Ramaswamy gave years ago.Indian-origin Vivek Ramaswamy, the GOP candidate running for Ohio Governor, always supported the H-1B visa program though not in its present form. Years ago, he once said that there should be no fixed cap on legal immigration and it should be a meritocracy. Admission to the US should only be based on skills and nothing else, he opined."It makes no sense to have legal immigration at a time when companies aren’t hiring, AI is replacing jobs, youth unemployment is high, and having a fragile economy. But they know this, what it’s really about is replacing American workers to maximize corporate profit," Nalin Haley commented out of his grudges against Ramaswamy."Meritocracy only works if it’s within a country. It can only be meritocracy for Americans. Otherwise, you’re no longer a country and reduced to a globalist entity," Haley commented. "They’re trying to take the GOP back to early 2010’s libertarianism and we can’t let that happen. The Republican Party must be a party supportive of the working class, uplifted by Americans and for Americans," he said.In December 2024, Ramaswamy triggered a major H-1B storm after he made a lengthy post explaining why America is failing to produce more STEM students, which is leading US companies to turn to foreign workers. In his explanation, Ramaswamy disparaged American culture of mediocrity and not taking academics seriously, unlike Asian culture. That rant earned Ramaswamy intense hatred from MAGA that have not forgiven him to date.After many a battle with groypers and MAGA, Ramaswamy stayed away from the immigration issue ahead of the election.Ramaswamy's race for Ohio governor against Democrat Amy Acton is now rated a toss-up by all three major forecasters, as he seeks to become only the third Indian-American governor in US history after Bobby Jindal and Nikki Haley.Polling averages on Saturday showed Acton ahead. Track the Vote put her at 48.5 per cent to Ramaswamy's 43.7 per cent, while PolitiKool had her at 48.4 per cent to his 43.8 per cent and noted a 3.6-point shift towards Acton over the past month. Vice President and Ramaswamy's friend JD Vance campaigned for him. "Vivek is an entrepreneur. He's a guy who hasn't just received a paycheck he signed a paycheck to. articles.title: Archbishop of the U.S. military says Catholic soldiers should not serve on firing squad
articles.summary: Archbishop Timothy Broglio, who oversees the Catholic Church’s pastoral services to Catholics in the U. military, is condemning the proposed livestream of th...
articles.body:
Archbishop Timothy Broglio, who oversees the Catholic Church's pastoral services to Catholics in the U.S. military, is condemning the proposed livestream of the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan.

Broglio, in a statement Monday, also stipulated that any Catholic soldier assigned to the U.S. Army firing squad should ask to be excused from that duty, which he described as contrary to the teachings of the church. He joins other Catholic leaders in speaking out against the death penalty and the livestream plans.

Hasan, an Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people in 2009 at Fort Hood in Texas, is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on Dec. 3.

Broglio recalled that he presided over the funeral of Michael Grant Cahill, the only civilian killed in that attack.

The crime committed by Hasan "was heinous, but does exposing the public to his execution serve any purpose?" Broglio asked.

"The US military generally enjoys a good reputation in the world," Broglio added. "Is there really a value to throwing them in the same boat with terrorists by broadcasting the image of the execution of a man in a wheelchair to the whole world?"

articles.title: British prop maker spends £9,000 building a backyard spaceship with a bar, seating that doubles as a bed and a screen showing distant planets
articles.summary: A British prop maker has turned a corner of his backyard into a science-fiction hideaway, complete with a bar, curved seating that doubles as a bed and a
articles.body: A British prop maker has turned a corner of his backyard into a science-fiction hideaway, complete with a bar, curved seating that doubles as a bed and a screen showing distant planets. In an interview with PEOPLE, Chester Walsh, 29, spent three months building the spaceship-inspired retreat at his home in Northamptonshire, with the project costing around £9,000. A lifelong fan of science fiction and comic books, he drew on several familiar spacecraft designs to shape the exterior and interior. What began as a personal project during renovations soon attracted millions of views online, giving Walsh a chance to showcase his craft while creating an unusual place to spend evenings with friends.How Chester Walsh turned his backyard into a Star Wars-inspired spaceshipWalsh, 29, has long been interested in science fiction and comic books, with the Star Wars universe providing much of the visual inspiration for his work. Before building the spacecraft, he had already experimented with transforming ordinary garden structures. At a previous home, he converted part of an old shed into a tiki bar and decorated a garden cabin used as an office and gym with science-fiction-inspired wall panels.The new project gave him an opportunity to take those ideas further. Renovation work at his house had temporarily left his usual workshop unavailable, so a substantial outdoor build offered a way to keep working while developing his portfolio. He wanted something that looked like a spacecraft but could also function as a comfortable place to spend time with friends.Rather than copying a recognisable ship in its entirety, Walsh combined details from several fictional spacecraft and other science-fiction settings. He researched reference images and prepared three-dimensional models before construction began. The overall shape drew inspiration from the Intersystem Transport at Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge, while the interior would incorporate familiar elements from other parts of the franchise.Building the spaceship took three months and around £9,000The construction started with the less glamorous work of preparing the ground. Walsh excavated the site, laid a sub-base and arranged for a reinforced concrete foundation to be poured. He then worked with the glamping pod company Made of Bits to develop a timber frame to his specifications.The structure rests on approximately 100 pedestal supports. As well as allowing air to circulate beneath it, the arrangement helps give the building the appearance of hovering above the ground. Walsh covered the frame with 6mm plywood and a waterproof EPDM rubber membrane before shaping the exterior with EVA foam and adding fibreglass for strength and weather protection.Most of the work was completed by Walsh himself. A registered electrician was brought in to run an armoured cable to the building and connect the electrical fittings and lights he had installed. His experience making props and working alongside his father, a builder, gave him a useful foundation, although the project still presented unfamiliar challenges.The budget had also grown beyond his initial hopes. Walsh originally set himself a ceiling of £10,000, while aiming to keep spending below £7,000. Once the concrete work, timber frame, fibreglass, electrical work, an interior monitor and numerous trips to the DIY retailer Wickes were included, the materials and construction costs came to roughly £9,000.Star Wars-inspired design of Chester Walsh’s garden spaceshipInside, Walsh used wood, Foamex, foam panels, paint and decorative finishes to create an environment that felt distinct from an ordinary garden room. The design took considerable inspiration from the Millennium Falcon as it appeared in Solo: A Star Wars Story, when the spacecraft belonged to Lando Calrissian rather than Han Solo.That version of the ship appealed to Walsh because of its cleaner appearance. The influence can be seen in the oval doorway and the panels surrounding it, as well as the ceiling, where white sections with rounded edges contrast with a black background. Elements inspired by Ahsoka Tano's spacecraft also feature around the entrance.The curved seating booth is another central part of the design. It follows the shape of the interior and provides a place for guests to sit together, rather than dividing the space into rows of separate seats. It is also long enough for one person to sleep on, making it possible to use the spacecraft as an occasional overnight retreat.Other details come from different corners of the science-fiction world. Walsh looked to the Death Star for lighting ideas and drew on the design of Disney's former Star Wars: Galactic Starcruiser when choosing the flooring.How Chester Walsh made his backyard spaceship a functional social spaceThe spaceship was designed to serve a practical purpose alongside its decorative one. A small bar provides storage for drinks, with a table Walsh found on Facebook Marketplace fitting the setting well enough to become part of the finished interior.Walsh recessed a monitor behind the wall panels and positioned it to line up with a false windshield. Footage of outer space and distant planets plays on the screen, giving visitors the impression that they are looking out from inside a spacecraft. The effect helps connect the different elements of the room. Without the screen, the curved seating, lighting and futuristic panels would still establish the theme, but the moving images give the apparent window a function beyond decoration.Walsh said, “My favorite feature is probably the oval doorway and surrounding paneling overall.” Visitors, however, have tended to respond to the whole structure rather than singling out one particular detail. Friends and family were familiar with his enthusiasm for ambitious projects, so their reactions were generally positive rather than surprised by the idea itself.One neighbour helped him excavate the foundation and later returned to see the completed build, taking photographs and videos. Another stopped by for a cup of tea and was impressed by the result.The backyard spaceship attracted millions of online viewsWalsh intended to document the construction from the beginning. Sharing the process offered a way to develop his social media presence, but he also hoped that showing what he could make might bring new customers and professional opportunities.As reported by the PEOPLE, He published more than 19 instalments following the build, covering the project from its foundations through to the completed interior. The detailed videos gave viewers a closer look at the work involved, including the practical decisions and techniques that went into shaping the structure.According to Walsh, the project has accumulated more than 2.5 million views across social media. The response also created a steady stream of questions from people curious about the construction, costs and materials.Rather than trying to respond individually to every comment, he points viewers towards the original series, which contains more detail about the different stages. Some people have told him that seeing the project encouraged them to try their own smaller-scale spaceship-inspired garden buildings.The attention has given the project a life beyond the original plan, although its main purpose remains personal. Walsh wanted a place where friends could gather without everyone having to stay in the house. If one group was talking indoors, another could spend time in the spacecraft.A friend ended up spending the night insideThe room has already been used for evenings with friends, including one occasion that demonstrated why Walsh had made the seating long enough to serve as a bed. After a few drinks, one friend decided to sleep inside the spaceship. Walsh discovered the following morning that he had gone through with it, spending the night curled up on the curved booth while the monitor continued displaying images of outer space.For Walsh, the incident was funny but also a satisfying demonstration of what he had intended to create. The structure was not meant to be a static prop that could only be admired from the garden. It was built to be occupied, with room for people to sit, talk, have a drink and, if the evening lasted long enough, stay overnight.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Abramovich’s close associate misled UK court in £1bn oil-fields case, documents suggest
articles.summary: Former Chelsea FC director, Eugene Tenenbaum, helped to manage the oligarch’s wealth.
articles.body:
One of Roman Abramovich's closest associates misled a UK court to help secure ownership of Siberian oil fields, leaked documents seen by the BBC suggest.

Eugene Tenenbaum, a former director of Chelsea Football Club, helped to manage the billionaire's wealth at the time of the case in 2008, which Abramovich won.

Tenenbaum was giving evidence during proceedings taken against Abramovich by a company owned by another Russian billionaire, who was claiming the oil fields had been stolen from him and other investors.

The leaked documents now suggest there was a premeditated attempt by Abramovich to reduce the value of the other investors' stake in the Siberian venture.

Roman Abramovich's lawyers say their "client denies all the allegations made against him".

Lawyers for Eugene Tenenbaum say he "denies in the strongest terms any suggestion that he committed perjury or contempt of court".

The 2008 court case centred on the ownership of Siberian oil fields being developed jointly between Abramovich's company, Sibneft, and the Russian subsidiary of the British company, Sibir Energy PLC, owned by Russian billionaire Chalva Tchigirinsky.

Sibneft contributed money, while the subsidiary Yugraneft provided the licences for the oil fields.

Their partnership - which became known as Sibneft-Yugra - ended acrimoniously.

Sibir's 50% interest in the joint venture had been diluted, or reduced, to less than 1%. It said this had been done without its knowledge.

Unsuccessful attempts to sue Sibneft in both Russia and the British Virgin Islands led to the court proceedings in London.

At court in 2008, Yugraneft claimed "to have been the victim of a massive fraud directed by Mr Abramovich", as a result of which it had suffered a loss of "not less that $2 billion", which in 2008 was worth about £1bn.

But Abramovich's team claimed that Yugraneft had been unable to repay loans of more than $30m, so lost its right over the shares.

Abramovich won the case on a number of fronts, including that Yugraneft's case had been an abuse of process.

However, Panorama has uncovered new evidence suggesting the court was misled, in a joint investigation with the Bureau of Investigative Journalism .

The evidence is contained in a leak of documents about Abramovich's finances and the operations of a network of offshore companies administered from Cyprus between 1995 and 2022. It raises serious questions about the integrity of some of the oligarch's professional advisers.

We have already found that the world's biggest accountancy firm, Deloitte, helped in falsifying documents to hide his wealth and evade tax.

The BBC and media partners including the Guardian, Paper Trail Media, the Organised Crime and Corruption Reporting Project and the Cyprus Investigative Reporting Network - as well the Bureau of Investigative Journalism - have been reporting on the leaked files since 2023 as part of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists' Cyprus Confidential investigation .

In the High Court, lawyers for Yugraneft argued the case should be heard in London, and that Tenenbaum, who was based there at the time, must have been aware of the dilution of Yugraneft's interest.

But Tenenbaum denied this and told the court "he only became aware of Sibneft-Yugra in Spring 2004".

He also testified he had "searched" his "files, emails and documents from 2002 to 2004" and had in his "possession no records or documents or other communications that relate to Sibneft-Yugra".

But the leaked documents suggest he misled the court.

They show that in October 2003, months before Tenenbaum said he first became aware of Sibneft-Yugra, he had authorised Abramovich's purchase of shares in the joint venture.

Two months later, Tenenbaum authorised another financial deal related to Sibneft-Yugra.

Andrew Mitchell KC, an expert in financial services law, told Panorama that it would be "very serious" if Tenenbaum's 2008 evidence was false and that it could "range from being perjury, to an attempt to pervert the course of justice, to being a contempt of the court".

Tenenbaum's lawyers told us "he gave his evidence honestly and in good faith" and that he "cannot recall the context or detail of documents" more than 20 years old.

The judge made clear in his 2008 judgement that Tenenbaum's knowledge of the Sibneft-Yugra deal would not have made a difference to his decision, however the leak also suggests some of the documents presented by Abramovich's legal team to the High Court had been falsified.

One of the agreements was dated August 2003, but appears not to have been created or actually signed until 2007.

Abramovich's team had argued in court that Yugraneft's interest had been diluted because of the need for finance for the joint venture.

They claimed Tchigirinsky had approached them "in the spring of 2002" with a view to new financing arrangements. Tchigirinsky denied this was the case.

The leaked documents show that before then, in January 2002, Abramovich's Russian associates had already prepared a bundle of documents.

They included agreements under which two Abramovich companies would acquire shares in Sibneft-Yugra, increasing his stake and diluting Yugraneft's.

This evidence suggests they were already planning to dilute Yugraneft's interest and that the argument they used in court about financing was a smokescreen.

Lawyers for Abramovich said: "The Judgment made no finding that the dilution was premeditated", or that it was "fraudulent". They added: "The Judge found that our client received no property belonging to Yugraneft, and that no Yugraneft asset could be traced into his hands."

articles.title: A British editor paid L.S. Lowry just £10 for ‘Going to the Mill’ in 1926 and kept it in the family for almost a century; 99 years later, the early industrial painting went to auction and sold for £805,200
articles.summary: A rare LS Lowry painting, 'Going to the Mill,' bought for just £10 in 1926, has sold at auction for over £805,000, marking a remarkable return on investment and celebrating Lowry's legacy in British art.
articles.body: A British newspaper editor bought an LS Lowry painting for just £10 in 1926 and kept it in his family for almost a century. Now, 99 years later, the early industrial scene has sold at auction for £805,200, including the buyer’s premium, after remaining in the same family’s collection throughout that period, The Guardian reported.The painting, Going to the Mill, was sold at Mall Galleries in central London on Friday, 2 May last year. Created in 1925, it was purchased directly from Lowry by Arthur Wallace, then literary editor of the Manchester Guardian. Although the work was marked at £30 on the back, the artist agreed to let Wallace have it for £10.How Lowry sold the painting for £10Wallace’s grandson, Keith, recalled how his grandfather acquired the work. According to him, Lowry proposed the lower price, after which Wallace wrote a cheque. The artist then offered him another painting.“Lowry said with great daring: ‘Could we say £10?’ and Grandpa wrote a cheque. Then Lowry wrote back to him saying: ‘I think I’ve charged you too much. Can I give you another one as well?’ So Grandpa got two Lowrys for £10,” Keith said.The second work, The Manufacturing Town, also went to the Wallace family. However, the family sold it several years ago, while Going to the Mill remained in its collection for nearly 100 years.Before its auction, Going to the Mill had been on long-term loan to Pallant House Gallery in Chichester.Auctioneer praises rare early Lowry paintingSimon Hucker, a modern and contemporary art specialist at the auction house Lyon & Turnbull, welcomed the result, highlighting the painting’s early date and the length of time it had remained in a single collection.“We’re absolutely delighted by the price achieved for this exceptional, early painting by Lowry, bought from him when he was a virtual unknown,” Hucker said.“There are few artists who become a household name in Britain and Lowry definitely falls into this category.”Hucker also described Going to the Mill as an example of Lowry’s distinctive approach to depicting industrial life. Rather than treating his figures as simple details within a scene, the artist used them to convey ideas about the experience of living in a crowded city.“Going to the Mill is the epitome of a 1920s Lowry, the period when he becomes a unique voice in British art,” Hucker said.He added that it was particularly rare for a painting of this kind to have remained in one collection for almost a century.Lowry’s depictions of industrial BritainLowry became known for paintings of industrial communities in north-west England, including scenes featuring factories, mills, terraced streets, chimneys and crowds moving through urban spaces.His work often captured the contrast between the energy of industrial cities and the loneliness of the people who lived and worked in them. Although he is widely associated with his depictions of workers and urban crowds, his output also included portraits, seascapes, landscapes and imaginative works.His recognition grew over time. Lowry received limited public attention early in his career, with his first solo exhibition in London taking place in 1939. He later became one of Britain’s best-known artists, and an arts centre in Salford was named after him.Previous saleThe £805,200 sale of Going to the Mill adds to the strong auction results achieved by Lowry’s work. In 2024, his painting Sunday Afternoon sold for almost £6.3 million at auction.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
articles.summary: Mitte, who lived with cerebral palsy, starred as Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series.
articles.body:
US actor RJ Mitte, best known for his role as the defiant son of drug kingpin Walter White in the drama series Breaking Bad, has died aged 34.

"It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," his representative told the BBC.

He died in Brownsville, Texas. No immediate cause of death was provided.

Mitte, who lived with cerebral palsy, drew on his own experience for his role as Walter White Jr in the Emmy-winning drama series starring Bryan Cranston and Aaron Paul. He earned a Screen Actors Guild Award in 2014 for his work on the series.

"Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," his representative Sean Reilly said in a statement to the BBC.

Mitte also served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children's.

He created The Mitte Foundation as well, to support philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, using his platform "to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities", Reilly said.

Breaking Bad aired on US cable broadcaster AMC for five seasons from 2008 to 2013.

The anti-hero drama created by Vince Gilligan earned a whopping 58 Primetime Emmy nominations and won 16, including two for Outstanding Drama Series in 2013 and 2014. It is widely credited as being one of the best US TV series of the 21st century.

Cranston plays a high school chemistry teacher in New Mexico who turns to a life of crime to support his family after a cancer diagnosis. As he descends deeper into the underbelly of the meth trade, he drifts further from his son, Walt Jr, who made his displeasure known with levity through much of the series.

Mitte, who grew up in Louisiana, was a young teen when he auditioned for the breakthrough role after moving to Los Angeles to support his younger sister's acting career in 2005.

He has previously said that his first audition in Los Angeles was for a California state public service announcement for an anti-meth commercial.

"Fast forward to auditioning for Breaking Bad, which is still, in my opinion, an anti-meth thing because it doesn't end well for anyone," he said on the Joe Vulpis Podcast earlier this month.

His character was based on Gilligan's late friend with a more severe case of cerebral palsy who used forearm crutches, which Mitte did not require.

He played the role with honesty and accessibility, cracking jokes as a teen whose health condition was never mentioned in the series.

After rising to prominence with the series, Mitte fought for more varied roles and complex depictions of characters with disabilities, both visible and invisible.

"Whenever awards season rolls around, we always hope to see a diverse group of projects that reflect all of us, in body and mind," he told the BBC in 2021 .

"Watching the awareness grow around disability representation has been great to see, but breakthroughs sometimes come in pieces and moments instead of larger change," he said.

Mitte's other on-screen credits include Hannah Montana, Switched at Birth, Westhampton and his latest project, Talking to Strangers, which came out earlier this year.

articles.title: Qantas flight grounded after bedbug outbreak
articles.summary: The flight from Italy to Australia was cancelled after passengers on the plane's previous journey complained of bug bites.
articles.body:
A Qantas flight from Italy to Australia was cancelled on Saturday, after an outbreak of bedbugs on the plane.

During the previous flight on Friday - a nearly 17-hour journey from Perth to Rome - some passengers had complained that they were being bitten by bugs, according to the Sydney Morning Herald.

They were reportedly given antihistamines to help ease the itch of the bites, but supplies ran out.

The Boeing 787 Dreamliner had to be grounded for "a deep clean", a Qantas spokesperson told the BBC.

"We sincerely apologise to customers for the cancellation of Saturday's Rome to Perth service, which allowed our engineers and maintenance teams to carry out a deep clean of the aircraft after an issue was identified on a small number of economy seats," the spokesperson said.

All affected customers were provided with accommodation and were rebooked on alternative flights within 48 hours of their original departure, the carrier said.

Bedbugs are small, wingless parasites that can live on clothes, furniture and bedding. Their bites can be itchy but they do not usually cause more serious health problems, the NHS website says .

But they can be difficult and expensive to get rid of. Treatment includes washing all bedding, clothing, and household materials like curtains on a hot wash and tumble dry, or they can be put in plastic bags in a freezer for three or four days.

Bedbugs causing travel chaos is not unusual - less than two weeks ago, several Southeastern train services in England were cancelled after drivers discovered the creepy-crawlies in their cabs.

In 2017, British Airways apologised to a family travelling from Vancouver to London, after they were left covered in bug bites from an overnight flight.

And Turkish Airlines faced with a PR nightmare last year after the New York Times reported of several instances of bedbug infestations on its planes - and allegations at the time that the airline did nothing about it.

articles.title: A Hertfordshire plan proposed 3,750 homes at Well End, but after public consultation the council dropped the entire extension as part of a wider removal of 6,752 planned homes from its local plan
articles.summary: A proposal to build 3,750 homes between Borehamwood and Shenley has been removed from Hertsmere Borough Council’s emerging Local Plan following public
articles.body: A proposal to build 3,750 homes between Borehamwood and Shenley has been removed from Hertsmere Borough Council’s emerging Local Plan following public consultation, according to the council’s September 29 announcement and its updated planning documents. The decision forms part of a wider revision that has taken four major housing extensions, with a combined capacity of 6,752 homes, out of the proposed plan. The Well End development was among the sites reconsidered after residents, community groups and other stakeholders raised concerns during a six-week consultation held between April 16 and May 29, 2026. The council said it had reviewed thousands of submissions before revising its proposals, according to The Borehamwood Post. Alongside Well End, the council has removed the proposed Mutton Lane extension in Potters Bar, which was earmarked for 1,750 homes; Compass Park in Bushey, planned for 802 homes; and land at Battlers Green Farm in Radlett, which had capacity for 450 homes. Together, the four sites account for 6,752 proposed homes. The changes represent a significant revision to the borough’s development strategy, although they do not mean Hertsmere has abandoned its wider housing plans.Thousands of responses shape revised housing proposalsThe consultation drew 6,374 individual responses, according to the consultation figures reported by The Borehamwood Post. Of these, 4,733 were based on templates prepared by community groups, highlighting the role organised local campaigns played in the process. Residents had raised concerns about the scale of proposed development and whether roads, schools, healthcare services and other infrastructure could adequately support additional housing. The council’s revised plan retains provisions for community facilities, including schools and medical centres, at selected development sites.The removal of Well End is particularly significant for the area between Borehamwood and Shenley, where the proposed extension would have brought thousands of additional homes to land outside the existing built-up area. However, the decision applies to the council’s emerging Local Plan rather than ruling out every future development proposal. Individual planning applications can still be submitted and considered through the planning system.Revised plan still includes 14,390 homesDespite dropping the four extensions, Hertsmere’s proposed Local Plan retains capacity for at least 14,390 net additional homes between 2026 and 2041. The figures are outlined in the council’s Regulation 19 plan and were also reported by planning news publication Planning Geek on October 8.Borehamwood and Elstree account for 3,413 homes, the largest share among the borough’s areas. Potters Bar has provision for 3,049 homes, followed by Bushey with 2,793 and Radlett with 2,635. A proposed new settlement at Bowmans Cross accounts for another 2,500 homes during the plan period, with the longer-term development expected to accommodate at least 5,000 homes in total.The remaining proposals include redevelopment and higher-density housing on existing urban sites, alongside selected development on land around the borough’s towns. The council has also identified provisions for new schools, healthcare facilities, transport improvements and green spaces to support growth.Local Plan enters formal consultation stageHertsmere councillors approved the publication of the revised plan at an extraordinary full council meeting on October 7. The Regulation 19 publication period opened the following day, giving residents, businesses and other interested parties six weeks to submit formal representations.The consultation closes at 11.59pm on November 19, 2026. Comments must address whether the proposed plan complies with legal requirements and whether it is sound, with any suggested changes explained. Following the consultation, the plan is due to return to the full council for consideration before submission for independent examination by the government’s Planning Inspectorate. The council is aiming to submit it by December 31, 2026, to remain within the existing plan-making system.Although the removal of Well End and the three other extensions marks a substantial change to Hertsmere’s housing strategy, the borough’s wider development programme remains in place. The next stage will determine whether the revised proposals meet planning requirements and can proceed towards adoption.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Dianna Russini could have a hard time returning to media following Mike Vrabel scandal
articles.summary: Dianna Russini reportedly hired crisis publicist Melissa Nathan to navigate past the Mike Vrabel scandal as she seeks a return to sports media.
articles.body: Dianna Russini has not made a public statement since announcing her resignation from The Athletic in April, following a series of leaks that showed her spending time privately with New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. Perhaps most bizarrely, TMZ reported that it had obtained records from a private boating trip involving the two six years earlier, months before the former NFL reporter gave birth to her first child. According to the New York Post, Russini is now seeking a return to the media. She recently hired crisis publicist Melissa Nathan to help her "navigate past the Mike Vrabel scandal." One could argue that Nathan's first piece of advice should have been not to leak that Russini hired a crisis publicist. On the surface, we are skeptical that any serious journalism outlet would hire Russini as an NFL reporter, a position she held for more than two decades. Rumors shape perception, and perception often becomes reality. The perception surrounding Russini is that she obtained information unethically because of an inappropriate relationship with Vrabel, romantic or otherwise. Any significant story she breaks would invite questions about how she obtained the information. The controversy could also make sources more reluctant to provide her with sensitive information. That said, Russini did not hurt anyone. At worst, she violated a basic journalistic ethical standard by failing to disclose a close personal relationship with an NFL coach she covered professionally. Her entire career does not deserve to end because of that. She may simply have to transition into a different role. Fantasy football analyst Matthew Berry told OutKick in August that he would "consider" signing Russini as an analyst for his media company, Fantasy Life. Dave Portnoy has also expressed interest in bringing her to Barstool Sports as a personality. MATTHEW BERRY HAS HAD TALKS WITH ESPN ABOUT A RETURN, FOLLOWING PAT MCAFEE MODEL There could be other suitors, depending on the price. The larger question is how much interest Russini could sustain as a personality. There would undoubtedly be initial curiosity. Nearly every sports and culture website would aggregate whatever she said about the photos and reports involving Vrabel. But that curiosity has a shelf life. Is she funny, engaging, and entertaining enough to become a star in the podcast space? Recent history suggests that such a transition is hardly automatic. The migration from traditional sports media to independent digital ventures has produced decidedly mixed results. Matthew Berry, Shannon Sharpe, Jason Whitlock, and Josh Pate have built substantial audiences and businesses outside the traditional sports-media structure. Others, including Skip Bayless, Bomani Jones, and Cari Champion, have struggled to replicate the relevance they enjoyed in more prominent roles. Russini also faces an obstacle they did not. None of them had to reinvent themselves after allegations that called into question the nature of their relationship with a prominent football coach. articles.title: Tyeb Mehta's 'Rickshaw Puller' fetches record 69 crore
articles.summary: In 2002, a Tyeb Mehta triptych aptly titled Celebration, from The Times of India collection, set off quite a party in the Indian art market when it became
articles.body: In 2002, a Tyeb Mehta triptych aptly titled Celebration, from The Times of India collection, set off quite a party in the Indian art market when it became the first Indian painting to cross the crore mark at auction. Though it came in the winter of his life, it was a remarkable milestone for an artist who had spent much of his life in a cramped one-room Bombay apartment that doubled as a studio by day and a bedroom at night. Since that landmark sale, prices for Mehta's paintings, including those featuring his signature bulls, have bull-dozed many old records. The latest is Rickshaw Puller, which fetched Rs 69.1 crore at Volte Una's inaugural auction, setting a world auction record for the artist. The sale surpassed Mehta's earlier personal high of Rs 61.8 crore, set by Trussed Bull in April 2025. Rickshaw Puller is now the fourth-most expensive Indian work of art ever sold at auction. The top spot belongs to Raja Ravi Varma (Rs 167 crore), followed by M F Husain in both second and third.Mehta first encountered rickshaw pullers as a young boy during summer holidays spent with his grandmother in Kolkata and they became a recurring theme. In his early works, the rickshaw puller was a sombre figure rendered in greys and deep reds. In the 2002 painting that set the record on Sunday, man and machine seem almost fused into one, yet one can feel the physical exhaustion of hauling passengers through the city's sweltering streets.The record is particularly striking for an artist known for his exacting standards, who routinely destroyed works he considered unworthy. It also marks a significant debut for Volte Una, a new auction house built around an unusual premise: offering one major work at a time rather than multiple lots in a single sale. The format is designed to give collectors time to engage closely with each artwork before bidding, with an emphasis on privacy."Why should a masterpiece be lost in a crowd? This way, we could expose Tyeb Mehta's painting to the most serious and discreet collectors globally in private settings," said Tushar Jiwarajka, founder of Volte Una. "We have introduced a business model that allows traditional buyer's premium to be significantly reduced, cutting transaction costs for both buyers and sellers."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Agencies flagged security concerns over satellite internet of foreign operator

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The challenge of regulating a satellite internet service controlled by a foreign operator is a key concern for Indian authorities as Elon Musk continues to target govt, alleging that Mukesh Ambani’s influence over it has been the main factor behind the SpaceX-run Starlink, owned by him, not being given a licence to offer its services in the country.Sources said that key ministries entrusted with security issues, including home and defence, besides intelligence agencies had flagged these challenges before the parliamentary committee on communication and information technology, which had taken up the matter.They further noted that authorities often resort to localised internet shutdowns when confronted with law and order challenges, including due to communal tensions, to curb the spread of “inflammatory” messages through social media platforms, and the emergence of satellite-linked internet service presents a tricky situation as its control remains abroad.There is also this concern about protection of data, which is increasingly gaining in salience for reasons of privacy as well as security.The committee chairperson, Nishikant Dubey, said nobody is against technology or foreign investment but security concerns must be addressed and there should be a level-playing field as well.Criticising Musk’s tirade on social media, Dubey said, “India cannot come under any foreign pressure. It has an independent policy and will do what is in the national interest.”The world’s richest person, who has drawn scrutiny for his sharp political stand on domestic affairs of different countries, has made a number of highly critical posts aimed at India, including one addressing Ambani as the prime minister, alleging that he was protecting his monopoly by not allowing SpaceX-run Starlink to operate in the country.Leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi has used his posts to sharpen his attack on govt for allegedly favouring a few big corporates, prompting BJP to recall Congress’s earlier concerns over Starlink and accusing him of reflexively backing any foreign interest critical of govt.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Author David Baldacci helped turn food banks into places where families could also find books; his Feeding Body & Mind initiative has collected and distributed more than 1 million books
articles.summary: For many families, a visit to a food bank is about meeting an immediate need: putting meals on the table.
articles.body: For many families, a visit to a food bank is about meeting an immediate need: putting meals on the table. Author David Baldacci and his wife, Michelle, wanted to add something that could nourish another part of family life, too. In 2008, their Wish You Well Foundation partnered with Feeding America to launch Feeding Body & Mind, a programme that collects new and gently used books and distributes them through food banks. Baldacci’s website says the initiative has collected and delivered more than one million books to families in need. The idea is straightforward: food helps sustain people today, while books can encourage learning, imagination and literacy over time. It has also given food banks a way to offer families something beyond groceries.Bringing books to food banksFeeding Body & Mind grew from the Baldaccis’ wider commitment to literacy. David and Michelle established the Wish You Well Foundation to support family and adult literacy programmes in the United States. Their partnership with Feeding America connected that work to a national network of food banks already serving families experiencing hunger.The programme addresses what its organisers see as connected challenges. Food insecurity can place pressure on families, while limited access to books and literacy resources can make learning harder. Feeding Body & Mind does not treat books as a substitute for food assistance. Instead, it brings the two forms of support together, so families visiting a food bank can also find reading material to take home.The Gaithersburg Book Festival’s profile of the programme explains its guiding idea: food can help keep a person alive, while stronger literacy skills can help create opportunities and challenge poverty. The initiative’s name captures that belief, linking nourishment for the body with resources for the mind.A book to take homeThe programme collects both new and gently used books. Rather than sending them to a central library, it distributes them through local food banks and community feeding programmes. This model lets books reach families in familiar places where they are already seeking assistance.The project has also invited readers to take part directly. At some of Baldacci’s book signings, supporters have been encouraged to bring books and place them in collection boxes. When a box is full, the Wish You Well Foundation arranges for the books to be sent to a nearby food bank, so donations can benefit families in that community. That local element matters. A donated book can become a child’s first book of their own, a story shared at bedtime or a resource for an adult building reading skills. The programme does not assume every family needs the same titles, but it creates a chance for readers to choose books that interest them and take them home. A book is a modest object, yet having one available can make a difference in a household where buying extra reading material may not be possible. For children, books can support curiosity and language development. For adults, reading materials can offer practice, entertainment and a way to share stories across generations.From a novelist’s idea to a national effortBaldacci is best known for his bestselling thrillers. His official biography says he has published dozens of novels for adults and young readers, with his work translated into more than 45 languages and published in over 80 countries. But his interest in literacy extends beyond his books and publishing career.The idea behind Feeding Body & Mind grew from recognising that reading resources are not equally available to every family. Food banks already provide an essential service, but they can also become a point of connection for other kinds of support. By working with Feeding America, the Wish You Well Foundation could reach families through a network with local relationships across the country.In its early years, the effort relied on book drives and partnerships with publishers and community organisations. A 2007 profile in Washingtonian reported that Baldacci asked people attending his book events to donate new or gently used books. The initiative had collected 35,000 books in its first three months, showing how a simple request could quickly draw public participation.The programme has since grown far beyond those early collection boxes. Baldacci’s website reports that more than one million books have now been collected and distributed through food banks to families in need.Why literacy belongs in the conversationThe programme’s premise is that hunger and literacy should not be treated as unrelated issues. A family may need food today, but access to books and reading support can also shape a child’s opportunities over time. Food banks are not schools or libraries, yet they can offer a practical route for sharing books with families who may otherwise have limited access to them.That does not mean a book alone can overcome poverty or replace formal education. Feeding Body & Mind works alongside other services and support systems. Its contribution is narrower but meaningful: it helps put books into homes through a channel families already use.For children, a book can invite a parent or caregiver to read aloud, create a shared routine and make stories part of daily life. For adults, reading materials can support confidence and encourage continued learning. These benefits are not always easy to measure in a single visit, but they reflect the longer view of literacy that underpins the programme.A million books, one family at a timeThe more than one million books distributed through Feeding Body & Mind represent a cumulative effort by donors, volunteers, publishers, food banks and the Baldacci family foundation. The number is impressive, but the initiative’s impact is ultimately experienced in individual homes, where a child discovers a story or a family finds a new reason to read together.The programme has helped food banks become more than places where families collect groceries. Through the partnership, they can also offer books that encourage reading and learning. That extra resource does not diminish the importance of food assistance. It recognises that families have needs beyond the immediate meal.David and Michelle Baldacci’s initiative began with a simple connection between nourishment and literacy. More than a million books later, that idea continues to travel through food banks and into homes across the United States.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Panel to address grievances of sugarcane growers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Govt Monday announced establishment of a high-level committee within a week to address the grievances of sugarcane farmers over discrepancies
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt Monday announced establishment of a high-level committee within a week to address the grievances of sugarcane farmers over discrepancies in sugar recovery, weighment and payments. The announcement was made at a meeting chaired by agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan which was attended by farmers from Maharashtra and Karnataka.Chouhan and food minister Pralhad Joshi held detailed discussions with a delegation of farmers from the two major cane-growing states. About 80-90 farmers from different organisations attended, along with state ministers.The committee will comprise representatives of the Centre, Karnataka and Maharashtra govts, farmer organisations and sugar mills, besides subject-matter experts and scientists.With sugar mills set to begin crushing in the 2026-27 season, which started on Oct 1, farmers have sought a higher support price, citing rising production costs.They have also demanded that MSP of sugar be raised from Rs 31/kg to Rs 50/kg.The panel will examine technical aspects and submit its recommendations within a stipulated timeframeGet the latest India News and Live updates.
